business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Catalog Retail of Industrial Maintenance Hardware

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (predominantly Napoleonic French commercial law with Germanic administrative law elements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg – United States double taxation convention, as amended by the 2009 Protocol
Luxembourg – Germany double taxation convention, as amended by subsequent protocols
Luxembourg – China double taxation convention signed in 2019

Luxembourg maintains an active network of more than 90 bilateral investment promotion and protection agreements and 75+ double tax treaties, including with all EU Member States and major OECD counterparties

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal regulation of 20 April 2020 on RBE practical modalities; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and the Trade and Companies Register; CSSF AML/CFT regulatory framework applicable to supervised professionals
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (non-public central RBE; full access for judicial, AML/CFT and administrative authorities and listed obliged entities; legitimate-interest applicants may request limited access under Article 5 of the 2019 RBE Law)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or official registry extract of each direct corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Apostille countries, Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of each manager, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority or certified notary public in country of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or notarization and, only where required, Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature or Hague Apostille if the bank letter is to be used cross-border

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn declaration of no bankruptcy and criminal record extract for each proposed manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent court or public prosecutor's office in country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all managers, shareholders, UBOs and material intermediaries against the UN Consolidated Lists, EU Financial Sanctions Database, US OFAC SDN List, CSSF published freeze lists, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists. PEP status must be assessed for all UBOs and managers in accordance with FATF Recommendation 12; identified PEPs are subject to enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior-management approval. Adverse media and negative-information queries are documented in the AML/CFT file, and any suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing is reported to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online search and filing portal via www.lbr.lu and the Guichet.lu company formation assistant
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Luxembourg SARL name must be written in Latin characters. French, German, Luxembourgish, and other languages using the Latin alphabet are acceptable; non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin characters. The full corporate name must be distinctive and not misleading, must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, and must include the legal-form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée', 'S.à r.l.' or 'SARL'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Private Banking (requires CSSF authorisation)
Assurance / Insurance / Réassurance / Agent d'assurances (requires Commissariat aux Assurances authorisation)
Fonds commun de placement / SICAV / SICAF / Fonds d'investissement (requires CSSF authorisation)
Trust / Trustee / Fiduciary (regulated trust-services authorisation required)
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Marché réglementé (requires regulatory approval)
Établissement de monnaie électronique / Payment Institution (requires CSSF licensing)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A formal RCS rejection is issued in writing with stated reasons. Within 15 days of refusal, the applicant or its notary may file a corrective name-reservation request or submit written observations to the RCS. If the name remains refused, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within 40 days of notification; representation by a Luxembourg avocat à la Cour is mandatory at the appeal stage, and an alternative name may be submitted simultaneously without separate prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be used for correspondence in this low-risk B2B MRO catalog e-commerce sector, but the SARL must maintain a physical registered office address in Luxembourg and cannot rely solely on a P.O. box. The registered office must be stated in the articles of association and must allow statutory mail, notice service, and authorities to inspect corporate records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, estimated at approximately 12% annual probability for a non-regulated, low-risk B2B e-commerce SARL with clean PEP/sanctions screening and orderly accounting; the likelihood rises materially if Luxembourg tax residence indicators, treasury activity, or AML red flags emerge.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name clearance and RCS non-confusion negative certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS online search and certificate tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Luxembourg notarial statutory tariff and prevailing Chamber of Notaries market schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg corporate law firm / avocat à la Cour
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, fixed fee or EUR 250–450/hour

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization and apostille processing of foreign corporate and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs legalization office, foreign registries, and apostille authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular, apostille, and courier fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and corporate mailbox arrangement, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for physical registered-office, mail handling, and statutory correspondence services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of the bank account for paid-in share capital and issuance of bank certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank prevailing tariff for account setup and KYC file; no statutory notarial fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Title V, Articles 710-1 et seq. (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and on Accounting, as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and coordinated articles of association (statuts coordonnés), filed electronically with the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000; fully subscribed and fully paid in cash before execution of the notarial deed; funds deposited in the notary's escrow client account and released only after RCS registration. Contributions in kind require an independent auditor's report and full transfer of the asset.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company accepts the subscription of 12,000 shares of EUR 1.00 each, fully paid in cash, as evidenced by the notary's escrow certificate. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company is adopted at the address stated in the articles, and the Manager is authorised to execute the lease and related administrative formalities. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as Manager (Gérant) and [Name] as authorised signatory, each acting singly, with authority to open bank accounts and engage professional advisers. RESOLVED, that the Manager is instructed to complete RCS registration, RESA publication, VAT registration and all other regulatory filings, and to take all steps necessary to lawfully commence the B2B MRO catalog business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS through Luxembourg Business Registers / notary-assisted online submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request to the RCS naming the proposed corporate entity and stating the statutory object. Confirm that the name is not identical to or confusingly similar to an existing RCS-registered name. Retain the name clearance or reservation acknowledgement for inclusion in the draft articles.
required_dossiers: Copy of founder's passport or ID
Notarized power of attorney if founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, propose one to three alternative names and re-submit; instruct the notary to amend the draft articles accordingly before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Minimum capital subscription and escrow deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account at the chosen Luxembourg notary. Transfer the full minimum capital of EUR 12,000 from the founder's bank account into the account. Provide bank transfer evidence, KYC documents and a source-of-funds declaration. The notary holds the funds until RCS registration and then releases them to the company.
required_dossiers: AML questionnaire completed by each shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If funds are not credited or the AML file is incomplete, the notary defers execution until all KYC and source-of-funds requests are fully satisfied; if the transfer is rejected, repeat with corrected bank details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial deed and articles before a Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaire luxembourgeois / Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the Luxembourg notary for execution of the notarial deed of incorporation and the articles. Verify identities, share subscription list, capital escrow certificate and any corporate shareholder approvals. The notary authenticates the deed, obtains all signatures, and arranges any annexes or English translations for foreign parties.
required_dossiers: Notary escrow certificate confirming paid-up capital
Passport or ID of each shareholder and manager
Board or shareholder resolutions if a corporate shareholder exists
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects a legal defect, execute a rectificatory deed before the same notary; if a signatory cannot attend, execute a separate power of attorney and re-notarize that proxy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés via Luxembourg Business Registers electronic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary to file the executed notarial deed and coordinated articles with the RCS through the LBR electronic filing system. Pay the applicable filing fee. The RCS records the company, assigns the RCS business number, and arranges publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA). Obtain the RCS extract as proof of legal existence.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query or refuses filing, the notary submits a corrective brief or supplementary act within fifteen days; registration becomes effective on the date the cured filing is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, social security and administrative post-registration filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) via Guichet.lu; Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) if employing staff
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, apply for the Luxembourg VAT number through the eCDF/Guichet.lu portal and state the intended B2B electronic catalog retail activity. If employees will be hired, register as an employer with the CCSS. Notify the municipal administration of the registered office and update bank signatory mandates.
required_dossiers: Identification of managers and authorised signatories
Estimated turnover statement for VAT purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT queries the VAT registration concerning cross-border e-commerce, provide the contract forms, price lists and confirmation that no fixed establishment exists outside Luxembourg; align the effective VAT date accordingly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, Directorate General for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises and Commerce (not directly applicable to pure online catalog retail; relevant only if a physical warehouse is later opened)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None – no dedicated industrial or manufacturing operating licence applies to ISIC 4791 electronic catalog retail of industrial maintenance hardware; if a physical warehouse is operated, a commercial establishment authorization under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 may be required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – activity is not listed under the Luxembourg environmental impact assessment law of 15 May 2018; no EIA report or environmental operating permit is required for B2B MRO supplies e-commerce
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source discharge. If warehousing is added, comply with municipal sanitary sewer discharge rules, EU VOC and air quality thresholds, and Luxembourg waste handling requirements under the Law of 21 March 2012; hazardous or packaged MRO materials must be declared and removed by authorised waste collectors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No specialised civil defence permit applies to this low-risk activity. For any office or warehouse premises, obtain municipal fire safety conformity, electrical installation clearance, and workplace health and safety inspection by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) before employees begin work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for income taxes, and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; electronic portal: guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity without a fixed establishment in Luxembourg must apply for VAT registration on guichet.lu using Form 104 VAT. The entity must provide constitutional documents, proof of foreign VAT number, identity of the legal representative, and a description of taxable activities. If the entity has no establishment in Luxembourg and no local representative, the AEDT may require appointment of a fiscal representative authorized to receive tax assessments. The application must be submitted before any taxable supply is made in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. A SARL is inherently subject to entity-level corporate income tax. Available statutory elections include: VAT group registration (assujetti unique), fiscal unity for corporate income tax purposes in respect of 95%+ owned resident subsidiaries, and group loss relief elections. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD must be considered for cross-border payments.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small enterprise exemption; however, non-established suppliers generally cannot rely on this exemption and must register from the first euro of taxable supply unless an EU one-stop-shop or special scheme applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg mandates PEPPOL-compliant electronic invoicing for all invoices issued to central and local public authorities. There is no general real-time fiscal clearance requirement, no mandatory API-based clearance for B2B invoices, and no digital stamping regime. B2B suppliers must ensure authenticity, integrity, and legibility of electronic invoices and retain them in VAT-compliant form.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies to the sale and dispatch of goods to destinations outside the EU, provided the supplier obtains and preserves documentary evidence that the goods left EU territory within the legally prescribed period, generally within three months of the supply. Offshore services provided to a recipient established outside the EU qualify for zero rating under Luxembourg VAT law where the place-of-supply rules confirm that the services are deemed supplied outside the Luxembourg/EU territory. The e-commerce MRO activity must maintain a complete export evidence file, including the export customs declaration and transport documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document - SAD) validated by Luxembourg Customs
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or CMR international consignment note
Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing FX receipt
Proof of customs entry or delivery acknowledgement in the destination country
Evidence of non-EU customer status or export order confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or substantively defective export zero-rating claims are disallowed by the AEDT, resulting in reassessment of VAT at the standard rate, default interest from the date the VAT was originally due, and administrative fines which may reach EUR 25,000 for serious violations. Deliberate non-compliance may expose the taxpayer to criminal penalties under Luxembourg tax law, including imprisonment for individual officers. The AEDT conducts targeted audits of export claims and requires retention of the full documentary bundle for at least ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) jointly with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking conduct, prudential supervision and anti-money laundering compliance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg operates under the euro and the EU framework of free movement of capital (Articles 63-65 TFEU, EU Capital Movement Directive). Both current account and capital account transactions are fully convertible with no administrative FX license or prior authorization. Profit remittance and dividend distributions require no exchange-control approval; the only structural conditions are standard corporate law formalities: annual account filing, availability of legally distributable reserves, dividend withholding tax at 15% (subject to domestic exemptions or treaty relief), and submission of a Luxembourg tax residency certificate where beneficial ownership is asserted. No currency window, repatriation, rationing, or compulsory conversion constraints exist.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline for surrendering export receipts to the banking system and no mandatory conversion ratio for foreign currency earned on exports. A Luxembourg SARL may freely retain export receivables in EUR, USD, GBP, or any other convertible currency in domestic or EU-licensed bank accounts, provided the account is reportable for balance of payments statistics on a monthly or quarterly basis to the BCL.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EU-licensed Fintech and EMI providers, but Low for offshore digital EMIs. A Luxembourg SARL may open treasury accounts with CSSF-authorized payment institutions and electronic money institutions that hold an EU passport, yet those entities cannot take deposits and lack Luxembourg deposit guarantee coverage. EMIs are acceptable as secondary payment collection rails for B2B customers, but are not viable for capital escrow, trade LC issuance, or the primary cross-border clearing spine. Offshore EMIs based in Switzerland, the United Kingdom, Singapore, Hong Kong, or the United States cannot passport into Luxembourg under CSSF rules and present prohibited restrictions on accepting repayable funds, thus causing significant legal and liquidity risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Luxembourg law and CSSF AML/CFT practice, at least one authorized director and each ultimate beneficial owner must undergo a physical identity verification interview during the initial account opening. Remote video-identity is only admitted if the bank has been satisfied with a CPSP-certified video tool, an advanced electronic signature compliant with eIDAS, or a recognized notarial apostille protocol—never purely as a form of convenience. In practice, Luxembourg banks mandate physical attendance at a Luxembourg branch for the director(s) and for natural person UBOs, with the corporate pack in French or English, accompanied by certified/notarized translations, original articles of association, a valid LBR UBO extract, and a recent commercial register certificate (RCS).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity or nominee suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) UBO extract, full corporate structure chart, register of shareholders, signed and notarized UBO self-declaration, director identity documents, and a board resolution confirming direct beneficial ownership and absence of nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, PEP, or sanctions flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent World-Check / Dow Jones screening report, PEP status declaration for each director and UBO, source of wealth statements, certified passport copies, proof of residential address, and a legal opinion confirming no sanctions exposure or politically exposed persons requiring heightened clearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source of equity funds for capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transferring bank statements for the last 12 months, purchase/sale agreement, dividend distribution minutes, audited financial statements, tax filings with Luxembourg tax clearance, notarial capital subscription deed, and written confirmation of no tax evasion posture.

Commercial invoices, supplier contracts, bills of lading, Incoterms schedules, customs declarations, proof of export license/re-export authorization where applicable, and counterparty beneficial ownership and KYC certificates from the counterparty's bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital injections are executed as SWIFT MT103/MT202 wire transfers from the investing parent to the SARL's euro-denominated operational or escrow account at a Luxembourg tier-1 financial institution. No central bank approval is required, but the receiving Luxembourg bank will need the reference to the corporate registration number (RCSL), the capital increase deed, and the subscription statement. The bank will apply the BCL external statistics reporting code for direct investments; for EU cross-border transfers this is captured under the BCL monthly external position reporting, with the SARL commonly asked to confirm the economic nature of the payment in the purpose field: 'Capital subscription / equity injection'. The settlement rail is TARGET2 with instant euro finality.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments are cleared through SWIFT MT103 for direct vendor wire transfers, or through SWIFT MT700 for commercial letters of credit issued in favor of foreign MRO suppliers under UCP600. For EU counterparties, SEPA Instant Credit Transfers and TARGET2 are the standard rails. Every outbound MT103 must include full structured remittance data—invoice number, purchase order, Incoterms, and product description—to allow automatic TBML transaction filtering; Luxembourg banks will require invoice and shipping documentation to be uploaded for any trade payment when the amount exceeds the bank’s de minimis threshold, and all payments must be consistent with the submitted underlying contract to avoid an AML suspension.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with transferability restrictions (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) where EUR/CNY or EUR/INR is not freely tradable onshore
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) for maturing asset-liability positions in USD/EUR
Vanilla European currency options and combination zero-cost collars
FX deposits and foreign currency term deposits up to the SARL’s treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss, notes and, if applicable, management report) deposited with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the eJustice portal; publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the annual general meeting (AGM), and no later than seven months after the financial year end (e.g., 31 July after 31 December year end; AGM must be held by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 10,000 in addition to restitution costs; repeated failure empowers the public prosecutor to request court-ordered administrative dissolution and strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax (CIT) return combined with municipal business tax (IBT) and net wealth tax (NWT) schedules (Form 511 / e-filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); electronic filing via MyGuichet / MyTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Twelve months after the end of the taxable year (for a calendar-year SARL, deadline of 31 December of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the assessed tax, monthly default interest of 0.6%, to include a statutory surtax for non-compliance; persistent failure can trigger discretionary tax assessment and recovery enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the beneficial owner register (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RBE, filed through the eJustice platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the annual shareholders’ meeting approving the annual accounts; in any event, no later than the statutory deadline for the annual accounts filing (calendar-year SARL: by 31 July); share transfers must be reported within one month of the transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 125,000 per individual and up to EUR 250,000 for legal persons, plus imprisonment up to 6 months for directors; additional exposure to administrative sanctions and restriction on the exercise of rights through the RCS.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is compulsory for a sous-location SARL when at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce above 50 employees. Audit is also required if the company is part of a consolidated group, has public-interest status, or is expressly obliged by its articles of association.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the law of 19 December 2002 on trade register accounting records and annual accounts, as amended; IFRS is permitted for unlisted entities and mandatory for public-interest entities that prepare consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must submit a confirmation to the RBE annually even when no beneficial owner change has occurred; the confirmation is aligned to the date of the annual accounts approval and must be made within one month after that approval. Any transfer of shares triggers an interim 30-day filing with updated beneficial ownership information, regardless of size.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate standard rate (17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax in Luxembourg City; rate varies by commune)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% exemption on net IP income under Luxembourg patent/innovation box; tax exemption for participation incomes; 30% super-deduction for qualifying R&D; allowances for digital/e-commerce infrastructure; no separate digital services tax for MRO catalogue retail

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax return – Form 510 (Déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu pour sociétés); filed electronically through the Luxembourg tax administration portal eCDF (eTax) authenticated via LuxTrust
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; mandatory quarterly provisional tax payments based on prior year assessment
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., 31 May for calendar-year companies); automatic extension for filing through an approved tax adviser, generally until 31 December of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit reconciled to taxable profit: add-back of non-deductible expenses, removal of exempt income, and application of special deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Luxembourg-source business income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or fixed base; offshore central administration income is not taxable unless covered by treaty

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim 80% exemption on qualifying patent/software royalties; requires legal ownership or exclusive usage rights and active management in Luxembourg
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may claim only with a Luxembourg PE and substantive R&D function; limited to resident or PE tax accounts

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back fines, penalties, non-business gifts, 50% of board fees paid to directors, partially deductible entertainment expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE must apply the same add-backs to expenses incurred for the Luxembourg branch

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim current year offset against carry-forward tax losses; unlimited timing under Luxembourg law but restricted on a change of activity combined with ownership shift greater than 75%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a Luxembourg PE of a non-resident entity may only be offset against future Luxembourg-source income; terminal losses cannot be repatriated to the foreign head office absent specific treaty provision

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recover dividend/interest withholding taxes paid by Luxembourg payors and claim imputation credits; used to offset final CIT liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE should attach Form 166 and the foreign exemption application to avoid excess withholding; recoverable only within Luxembourg

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing interest accrues at 0.8% per month on the outstanding tax; late filing penalty surcharge up to 10% of assessed tax; ex officio assessment by the ACD with no right to further administrative deductions; repeated non-filing exposes directors to criminal prosecution and additional fines up to €25,000

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory corporate dividend withholding tax on distributions made by a Luxembourg SARL
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Qualifying shareholders must apply to the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD) for relief before distribution; submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate from the state of residence, proof of beneficial ownership, shareholding period and percentage, and the appropriate treaty/European Directive relief form (Form 166); EU parent-subsidiary directive eliminates WHT without any time delay for qualifying 10% shareholders after 12-month holding; treaty reductions generally range from 0% to 15% depending on the DTA
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law applies 0% withholding tax on most outbound interest and IP royalties paid by a Luxembourg business, subject to anti-abuse rules; treaty rates may further reduce or eliminate, typically 0%–5% for royalties and 0%–10% for financial interest, but the 2021 Luxembourg low-tax jurisdiction WHT of 20% can apply to payments made to associated enterprises located in EU-listed non-cooperative jurisdictions

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where the aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 100,000 per tax year; Master File is required for Luxembourg group entities belonging to a multinational group with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million; extended documentation triggers also apply for financing or royalty-rich structures above EUR 100,000 of intragroup interest/royalty flow
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Economic Substance Regulation in Luxembourg, but the general anti-abuse provisions and OECD/ATAD case law require substance: physical premises, qualified full-time employees, and decision-making in Luxembourg; pure shell structures are denied treaty benefits and DTA relief; IP-heavy traders must show active management, dept of R&D, and risk-bearing capacity under the Luxembourg patent box rules

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully filing a false corporate income tax return; omitting Luxembourg-source sales from the catalogue/e-commerce operation; fabrication of invoices; using an offshore intermediary to conceal taxable turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to €25,000 and imprisonment from 1 to 5 years; administrative assessment of the entire hidden tax plus late payment interest; penalties up to 10% of the deficient tax per late month; confiscation of the benefit and potential publication of the court decision
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or implement the fraudulent return are jointly and severally liable for the concealed tax, penalties, and interest; travel bans and freezing of personal assets may be issued; criminal conviction is not dischargeable in bankruptcy and can lead to disqualification from corporate management for up to 10 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Sham Business Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SARL with nominal capital, no real B2B MRO activities, no storage facility or personnel, and no business decision-making in Luxembourg; contractually routing all profit through tax-haven related parties without commercial rationale
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of corporate personality for tax purposes under Luxembourg GAAR; disallowance of treaty relief and EU directive exemptions; recharacterization of the SARL as a transparent entity or disposition by the tax administration; 5% to 25% correction penalties on re-assessed taxable profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable to third-party creditors under the doctrine of abuse of legal personality; personal restitution for unlawful distributions; court-ordered liquidation and legal action by the Luxembourg Public Prosecutor; criminal liability for fraud where intent is shown

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / KYC Failure in Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing credit-card or SWIFT wire payments without customer due diligence, failing to file suspicious transaction reports, mis-classifying the B2B e-commerce activity to avoid AML registration, or allowing shell customers to use the platform for money laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of worldwide turnover under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004; temporary suspension or revocation of the payment service licence; administrative seizure of funds; regulatory censure by the CSSF/CRF
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for AML breaches where they failed to establish adequate controls; civil damages to defrauded clients; criminal sanctions including imprisonment up to 5 years for laundering offences; travel bans and extradition possibilities under Luxembourg legal cooperation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Unjustified Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mispricing related-party sourcing of MRO hardware; operating with zero-margin or negative-margin intragroup supply chains; failing to prepare a Local File while cross-border related-party transactions exceed the EUR 100,000 threshold; using comparability adjustments without documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment with resulting tax plus late interest; penalty up to 25% of the under-assessed taxable income; in severe cases, the adjustment is combined with a 50% fraud penalty; denial of deduction for absent documentation where unable to demonstrate arm's length nature
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign transfer pricing documentation knowing it is false commit criminal tax fraud; joint and several liability for the additional corporate tax and penalties; prohibition from serving as director in a Luxembourg commercial company; imprisonment for repeated breaches; personal recourse orders by creditors in insolvency
